subject: Align calendars: 75-min ML serving workshop & success metrics
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Nguyen <alyssa@datahelix.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + next step: ML serving workshop

Hi Alyssa — great chat today, thanks for the time. A quick recap and a proposed next step so we can bring the right people together:

- Goal: Lock a 60–90 minute technical workshop focused on production inference (latency & throughput SLOs), model variants/quantization, and KPI alignment for your pilot.
- Outcomes we aim for: an ops runbook draft, recommended capacity footprint, and a short list of success metrics we can instrument during the trial.

Proposed workshop length: 75 minutes (split: 20m context & goals, 40m hands-on infra discussion, 15m next steps + action items).

Do any of these windows work for your team next week?
- Tue 2026-09-15, 09:30–10:45 PT
- Wed 2026-09-16, 13:00–14:15 PT
- Thu 2026-09-17, 16:00–17:15 PT

Attendees we suggest from Redwood: me (sales), Vivek (ML infra lead), and Priyom (solutions engineer) — we can tailor who attends based on which areas you want covered. Please confirm the DataHelix attendees (we assume an ML infra lead + product manager + security/ops if you'd like).

I attached a short proposed agenda (redwood-tdx-proposed-agenda.pdf) and a prep checklist link for your ops folks. If you prefer a different cadence or want a shorter, focused runthrough (60m), we can absolutely do that.

Thanks — once you confirm a slot I’ll send a calendar invite with a short pre-read and an optional Zoom recording permission.

Best,

Neha Kapoor

On Wed, Sep 9, 2026 at 6:03 PM Alyssa Nguyen <alyssa@datahelix.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Neha — good summary. We’d like to move forward with the 75-minute workshop.

Thanks, Alyssa — we’ll hold Wed 2026-09-16 13:00–14:15 PT as tentative. A few notes from our side so we can make the session prescriptive:

- Agenda tweak: 15m business context & constraints (you), 30m infra & footprint discussion (Vivek + Tom), 20m model serving patterns & fallbacks (Priyom), 10m action items + next steps.
- Fall-back strategies: we’ll bring recommended variant routing policies (regional fallbacks, smaller quantized variants) and a decision tree to guide automated switching when latency or error rates spike.
- Telemetry we recommend: tail latency p95/p99, token/sec throughput, batch size distribution, cache hit ratio, quantized vs full-precision execution time, cost per 1k tokens. We’ll provide a short telemetry template in the prep doc.

Prep attachment: tdx-prep-checklist.md (checklist + suggested pre-read links). Please have your ML infra lead share a short note on current peak qps and typical sequence lengths if possible — that will help us size recommendations.

If Maya can’t make it, a security engineer who can speak to network egress and key management is a fine substitute.

I’ll coordinate a calendar invite once Alyssa confirms the final attendees.

—Vivek Kulkarni
ML Infrastructure Lead | Redwood Inference
